title: Ancient Greece & democracy
examples: What were the main differences between Athens and Sparta?
How did the idea of democracy start in Ancient Greece?
Can you explain what a city-state is using an example?

explain.say: Today we will explore ancient Greece and its city-states. A city-state was like a self-contained small country.
Athens was a famous city-state known for its culture and ideas. They developed a very important system called democracy.
In Athenian democracy, the citizens had the right to vote on laws. This meant they had a say in how they were governed.
Sparta was another major city-state, but it focused more on military strength. Their citizens were trained to be excellent soldiers.
The legacy of Ancient Greece is huge for us today. Their ideas about law and self-rule still influence us.

draw.text: Legacy: Ideas of Law and Rule

explain.say: Think about a modern school council. It is like a small democracy. Students vote for representatives to make rules for the school.

faq.a: A city-state was a self-governing city that also controlled the surrounding land. It was like a small, independent country within a larger region.
asks: What is the definition of a city-state?
Did all Greek cities function as city-states?

faq.q: Who could actually vote in Athenian democracy?
faq.a: Only free-born male citizens were generally allowed to vote in the Athenian assembly. Women and slaves could not participate in voting.
asks: Were all people allowed to vote in Athens?
Who was excluded from Athenian voting rights?

faq.q: What was the main difference between Athens and Sparta?
faq.a: Athens valued arts, philosophy, and democratic debate, while Sparta was highly focused on military discipline and strength.
asks: Which city was more focused on fighting?

faq.q: How did the Greeks influence modern governments?
faq.a: The Greeks gave us foundational ideas about citizenship and the right of people to participate in their own laws. This is the root of democracy.
asks: Do we owe anything to the Greeks?
What is the lasting impact of Greek thought?

faq.q: Did all Greek city-states practice democracy?
faq.a: No, not all city-states practiced democracy. Some, like Sparta, had different forms of rule that emphasized military rule.
asks: Was democracy common in ancient Greece?
Did every Greek city have democracy?

facts: City-states were independent political units in Ancient Greece.
Athenian democracy allowed male citizens to vote on laws.
Sparta was famous for its rigorous military training system.
The Greek concept of citizenship influenced later political thought.

quiz.say: A self-governing city and its surrounding lands is best described as a:
quiz.why: This term accurately describes the independent nature of Greek political units.

wrong.1: An empire is usually ruled by a single powerful center over many lands.
wrong.2: While related, a republic is a specific form of government, not the general term for the unit.
wrong.3: Tribes were often groups of people, not necessarily organized political units with their own laws.

quiz.say: Which city-state was most known for its emphasis on arts and voting?
quiz.why: Athens is historically celebrated for its cultural achievements and democratic practices.

wrong.0: Sparta's primary focus was on military discipline, not arts or debate.
wrong.1: Thebes was another city-state, but Athens is the primary example for democracy.
wrong.2: Corinth was known for trade, but Athens is the key example for democracy.

quiz.say: If a group of people vote on a new law, they are practicing:
quiz.why: Democracy means rule by the people, which is shown through voting.

wrong.0: An oligarchy means rule by a small group of powerful people, not everyone.
wrong.1: A dictatorship involves rule by one person with no elected power.
wrong.3: A monarchy is rule by one king or queen, not by voting.
